item.title: NSCDC Smashes Border Gang Hideout In Ebonyi
item.description: Operatives of the Nigeria Security and Civil Defence Corps (NSCDC), Ebonyi State Command, have dismantled a criminal syndicate operating along the Ebonyi-Benue border, recovering an AK-47 rifle, live ammunition, and various dangerous items during a targeted sting operation. The operation, which targeted hideouts used by hoodlums and cult groups operating between Izzi Local Government Area in Ebonyi and neighboring Benue State, followed a week-long intelligence-gathering exercise. The raid was jointly executed by operatives from the Command’s Intelligence and Investigation Department alongside the State Commandant’s Special Squad. Briefing newsmen on Thursday at the Command Headquarters in Abakaliki, the State Commandant, Francis Nnadi, confirmed the success of the multi-location operation, highlighting the professional conduct of the officers during the raid on the fleeing suspects and their collaborators. During the sweep of the enclave, security operatives recovered the following items: 1 AK-47 rifle, 1 double-loaded magazine, 4 rounds of live ammunition, 1 locally-made pistol, 1 pump-action gun, 5 tactical knives, and assorted criminal charms. Issuing a strong warning to criminal networks operating within the state, Commandant Nnadi emphasized that the Command, in close synergy with sister security agencies, remains steadfast in wiping out criminality across Ebonyi. “I want to warn criminal elements ahead of the general elections to flee Ebonyi State. The Command, in conjunction with other sister security agencies, is fully prepared to rid the state of all forms of crime and criminality,” Nnadi stated. He further reassured residents in border areas and across the state of robust security coverage throughout the electoral season. “I want to assure residents of the border communities and the entire state of adequate security before, during, and after the elections.” “I urge the public to continue providing credible, timely information to assist security agencies in maintaining law and order,” he added. Manhunt operations are currently underway to track down and apprehend the fleeing suspects. The post NSCDC Smashes Border Gang Hideout In Ebonyi appeared first on Channels Television .

item.title: ADC Rejects Judgment Voiding Atiku’s Candidacy, Accuses APC Of Desperation To Cripple Opposition
item.description: The African Democratic Congress (ADC) has rejected the judgment by Justice Peter Lifu of the Federal High Court, Abuja, which sacked the Senator David Mark-led ADC leadership and invalidated the candidacy of former Vice President Atiku Abubakar. The party described the judgment as another desperate attempt by the ruling All Progressives Congress (APC) to cripple the opposition and deny Nigerians the right to choose their leaders in the forthcoming 2027 general elections. It added that the November 4 presidential campaign rally in Sokoto State sent the APC into panic. In a statement signed by its National Publicity Secretary, Bolaji Abdullahi, on Thursday, the party said the timing of the judgment, barely 24 hours after the massive turnout at the ADC presidential campaign rally in Sokoto, exposed what it considers the growing desperation of the APC. “We have reasons to believe that the judgment had long been written on this case. The Sokoto rally was simply a trigger that stampeded its delivery,” it stated. “Yesterday, Nigerians came out in their hundreds of thousands to demonstrate their support for the ADC and our promise of making life affordable for them. Today, they are being told that the party that they support and the candidates that they have supported at all levels could be erased by the stroke of a reckless judicial pen.” The opposition party questioned “whether those behind the flawed judgment” had considered its far-reaching implications for the country. It warned that the attempt to invalidate the party’s leadership could affect thousands of candidates contesting elections at the local, state and federal levels. “Do these people understand what they are playing with? This is not about Atiku Abubakar or David Mark. It is about the democratic rights of Nigerians to freely choose their own leaders. It is about the rights of thousands of candidates to participate in a democratic process,” it added. The ADC maintained that the judgment was legally indefensible and would be challenged through every available judicial process. “Our objection is particularly anchored on the subsisting judgment of Justice Musa Liman of the same Federal High Court, delivered on 2 July 2026 in Suit No. FHC/ABJ/CS/1637/2025, which affirmed the legitimacy of the David Mark-led NWC and directed INEC to recognise the leadership. It is a settled principle of Nigerian jurisprudence that a court of coordinate jurisdiction cannot sit on appeal over, review, vary or nullify the subsisting judgment of another court of equal jurisdiction,” it said. “The ADC, therefore, rejects any consequential orders founded on a determination that appears to disregard these fundamental legal principles. However, we await the Certified True Copy (CTC) of the said judgment to ascertain its precise terms, scope and operative orders.” Atiku (centre) is the presidential candidate of the ADC for the 2027 general elections. item.title: 2027: Court ruling strategy to weaken my support in north – Atiku
item.description: By Luminous Jannamike, Abuja Former Vice President Atiku Abubakar has accused the ruling All Progressives Congress, APC, of using Thursday’s Federal High Court judgment on the leadership of the African Democratic Congress, ADC, to frustrate his presidential ambition and contain the opposition party’s growing political influence ahead of the 2027 elections. Atiku said the ruling came barely 24 hours after thousands of supporters welcomed him to Sokoto for the launch of the ADC campaign, alleging that the development was part of a strategy to weaken his Northern support base and halt the spread of his campaign beyond the region. In a statement on Thursday by Phrank Shaibu, Director of Strategic Communication of the ADC Presidential Campaign Council, the former vice president insisted that the judgment would neither derail the party’s campaign nor diminish its appeal across the country. He said the Sokoto reception reflected Nigerians’ growing frustration with economic hardship and their desire for a change of government. “The people of Sokoto came out in their thousands because they are hungry for change and believe in our promise to make life affordable again. What we witnessed in Sokoto is only the beginning. The people of Kebbi will have their say, and so will Nigerians across the country as our campaign moves forward,” he said. Rejecting attempts to frame his candidacy as a Northern project, Atiku said the economic crisis confronting Nigerians had made his political message relevant across regional boundaries. “My roots are in Northern Nigeria, but my candidacy belongs to all Nigerians. There is a difference between being from the North and being a candidate only for the North. Hunger and hardship do not respect regional boundaries. Nigerians across the country are suffering under this government, and they deserve a leader with a credible plan to make life affordable again,” he said. Atiku alleged that the judgment was intended to disrupt the momentum of his campaign and weaken the opposition’s growing political reach. “The timing of this judgment is no coincidence. It is part of a strategy to weaken my support in the North and frustrate a campaign whose message is resonating across the country. But the ruling party’s greatest miscalculation is to assume that my support ends in the North. What we saw in Sokoto, what we will see in Kebbi and across the country, is the strength of a national movement,” he said. On the legal implications, Atiku questioned why the leadership dispute was reopened despite an earlier judgment by Justice Musa Liman of the Federal High Court, Abuja, in Suit No. FHC/ABJ/CS/1637/2025. item.title: Cristiano Ronaldo’s five great moments with Portugal
item.description: Cristiano Ronaldo announced his retirement from international football on Thursday to bring down the curtain on more than two decades in the Portugal shirt. He scored a record 146 times in a mammoth 234 appearances for his country having made his debut in 2003. Here are his five stand-out games with the Selecao. 2013: Outclassing Zlatan Having won the World Cup play-off first leg 1-0 against Sweden thanks to the iconic No. 7, Portugal headed to Stockholm for the return fixture. Ronaldo opened the scoring before Zlatan Ibrahimovic brought the sides level in the tie with a double in the Swedish capital. But the then Real Madrid attacker claimed Portugal’s spot at the tournament in Brazil by completing his hat-trick in two minutes. 2016: Tears before the joy Portugal reached the Euro 2016 final having failed to win a single group game. Ronaldo’s side went into the decider against hosts France in Paris searching for their first major international trophy and to make up for the past after losing to Greece on home soil 12 years earlier. The forward left the field injured and in tears after just 25 minutes before spending the rest of the game on the touchline cheering on his teammates. Eder scored the winner in extra-time to the relief of Ronaldo and 11 million Portuguese compatriots. 2018: One-man mission Fresh from winning three straight Champions Leagues with Real, Ronaldo faced Spain in Portugal’s World Cup opener in 2018. CR7 opened the scoring in Sochi with a penalty before grabbing a hat-trick, including a superb late free kick, to fire Portugal to a thrilling draw. 2025: 40 years young Three months after turning 40, Ronaldo helped Portugal to the Nations League final against Spain in Munich. He scored the winner over Germany in the semi-final before claiming the equaliser against Spain to send the decider to extra time. The Selecao eventually won on penalties, six years on from winning the same crown. 2026: Outplayed Croatia Following a lacklustre group stage, Ronaldo and Portugal faced Croatia in the last 32 of this year’s World Cup in Toronto. Despite the prospect of it being his final ever World Cup match, Ronaldo took control of things. He had an early effort chalked off for offside and Ivan Perisic put Croatia ahead, but Ronaldo equalised for Portugal from the penalty spot. Goncalo Ramos’ late header gave Portugal a memorable 2-1 victory and sent them into the last 16, where they lost to eventual winners Spain. item.title: Bank of England Lifts Rate For First Time Since 2023 To Fight Inflation
item.description: The Bank of England raised its benchmark interest rate to four percent on Thursday, the first increase in more than three years, as soaring energy costs push up global inflation. The central bank tightened borrowing costs by a quarter point, catching up with the US Federal Reserve and the European Central Bank in lifting rates since the start of the Middle East conflict. Along with Ukraine’s strikes on Russian refineries, disruptions to Gulf energy supplies owing to the US-Iran war have caused record-high diesel prices around the world. “There is now enough inflationary pressure in the pipeline caused by the rise in energy prices, that an increase in Bank Rate is warranted,” BoE governor Andrew Bailey said in a statement. “Today’s increase shouldn’t be seen as the first in an inevitable long sequence of hikes,” Bailey said. “But, unless the conflict in the Middle East is resolved, neither does it seem likely to be the last increase.” Bank of England Governor Andrew Bailey attends the Bank of England Monetary Policy Report press conference at Bank Of England in London on November 5, 2026. Photo by ALISHIA ABODUNDE / POOL / AFP Despite surging inflation, the bank upgraded its forecasts for UK economic growth in 2026 and 2027. The central bank now estimates gross domestic product to hit 1.6 percent this year and 1.3 percent next year. In July, it had forecast GDP output of 1.1 percent in both years. The BoE last raised its key interest rate in August 2023, and has kept the cost of borrowing at 3.75 percent since December. Britain’s annual inflation rate accelerated by more than expected in September, rising to 3.5 percent — well above the bank’s target of two percent. The BoE on Thursday said its central forecast saw UK inflation peaking at 4.9 in the second quarter of next year. Millions of Britons face a jump in energy bills from the start of next year, even after the government offered some assistance in its annual budget announcement last week. item.title: Troops rescue nine kidnapped victims, recover 108 livestock in Kebbi
item.description: By Kingsley Omonobi Troops of Operation Fansan Yamma have rescued nine kidnapped victims and recovered 108 livestock during security operations in Danko general area and Sabon Tunga and Binoni villages in Danko-Wasagu Local Government Area of Kebbi State. The Acting Military Information Officer, Captain Tamuno Siniveie, disclosed this in a statement on Thursday. He said troops of Sector 2 received a distress call on November 3, 2026, over an attack by suspected bandits who allegedly kidnapped residents and rustled cattle in the Danko general area. According to him, the troops immediately mobilised to the area and engaged the suspected bandits, forcing them to flee and abandon their captives. “Following the encounter, the troops rescued two kidnapped victims identified as Barbuga Bawashe, 26, and Barka Dakaji, 61. “The troops also recovered 34 cows and 74 rams,” he said. Siniveie added that in a related operation on the same day, troops rescued seven other kidnapped victims at Sabon Tunga and Binoni villages. He said the victims, who had reportedly been held captive for several months, escaped from their captors amid sustained military operations in the area. The rescued victims were identified as Muhammad Dogonta, 60; Zakari Yahu, 32; Basara Sheu, 10; Adam Shehu, 12; Hatsat Umar, 14; Albaria Hamsu, 12; and Yehusa Lawali, 35. The military spokesman said the rescued victims had been handed over to the District Head of Unashi for onward reunion with their families. He reaffirmed the commitment of the Joint Task Force North West, Operation Fansan Yamma, to protecting lives and property within its area of operations. He also urged members of the public to support security operations by providing timely and credible information to the troops. item.title: I now take English classes to speak fluently – MC Oluomo
item.description: The President of the National Union of Road Transport Workers (NURTW), Musiliu Akinsanya, popularly known as MC Oluomo, has disclosed that he is taking English lessons to improve his spoken communication. The transport union leader made this known while addressing Nollywood actor Adams Kehinde, popularly known as Lege Miami, and other attendees at a rally organised in support of President Bola Tinubu’s re-election bid. Speaking in Yoruba, MC Oluomo admitted that he and Lege Miami were not fluent in English, revealing that he had enrolled for lessons to improve his proficiency in the language. He also noted that despite travelling frequently to different countries, he had yet to become fluent in spoken English. “Neither of us speaks English fluently, so I am taking classes to improve. I travel around the world. I am a citizen of America,” he said. MC Oluomo further spoke about his children’s educational and professional achievements in the United States, noting that they were more proficient in English than he was. “My children can speak better than me. My children in the US are nurses, a doctor and an engineer,” he added. He explained that he sometimes handed the microphone to his children to speak on his behalf whenever he struggled to express himself in English. The disclosure comes amid previous public criticism of his spoken English, particularly in April 2025, when a video of him pronouncing the word “kudos” as “kundusi” while addressing union members in Abuja went viral. Responding to the criticism at the time, MC Oluomo acknowledged his limitations in the English language but maintained that fluency in the language did not determine one’s achievements. “Grammar won’t finish Nigeria. I might not understand the English language, but I understand Yoruba,” he said. He also challenged his critics to compare their achievements with those of his children, whom he described as highly educated and citizens of the United States and the United Kingdom. item.title: 2027: Opposition coalition demands audit of voter register
item.description: By Omeiza Ajayi, Abuja Nigeria’s opposition alliance, the Coalition for Democracy, formerly known as G100, has accused the ruling All Progressives Congress APC of rigging the rules before the votes, saying Nigeria cannot have free elections without free political competition. According to the coalition, APC is “systematically shrinking Nigeria’s democratic space” and demanded an independent forensic audit of the voters’ register before December 15. In a statement signed by Salihu Moh. Lukman on behalf of the coalition parties on Thursday, the group said the APC was “creating an electoral environment in which only the ruling party enjoys privileges that are deliberately denied to the opposition.” The coalition, which announced its decision to formally adopt the name Coalition for Democracy, replacing the old G100 Coalition, was formed after the 1st Opposition Summit on August 31, 2026, in Abuja. Its Central Leadership Committee CLC took the decision at a meeting in Abuja on Wednesday, November 4, 2026. The name, it said, reflects “the common commitment of its member parties to the defence of constitutional democracy, the rule of law and the protection of Nigerians’ fundamental political rights.” The CLC warned that, with barely 72 days to the January 16 elections, “the conduct of government institutions and security agencies raises serious questions about whether Nigerians will be allowed to freely choose their leaders.” According to the Committee, in the last 90 days alone, opposition supporters have been attacked in Kaduna, ambushed in Ibadan and attacked in Sokoto and Cross River. It added that hotels booked for opposition delegates have cancelled reservations, campaign offices have been sealed, and opposition billboards have been pulled down in Edo State “while those of the ruling party remain untouched.” In the Federal Capital Territory (FCT), the statement said opposition access to outdoor advertising “has reportedly been subjected to charges as high as N750 million.” The Committee also cited “one particularly disturbing incident” in which a local government chairman reportedly told residents to vote for the APC or leave their community. “The APC is not just trying to win the election. It is trying to decide the conditions under which everybody else must contest it. This is what happens when a ruling party begins to confuse its control of government with ownership of democracy. You cannot be a contestant and insist on writing the rules for your opponents,” it stated. The coalition expressed what it called “even greater concern” over the integrity of the voters’ register, noting that the Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC) failed to meet the statutory deadline prescribed by Section 19(1) of the Electoral Act 2026. item.title: FG seeks global investment to develop blue economy
item.description: By Folarin Kehinde The Federal Government is seeking increased access to international maritime investment, technical expertise and capacity-building opportunities to strengthen Nigeria’s participation in the global shipping industry and unlock the economic potential of its blue economy. Minister of Marine and Blue Economy, Adegboyega Oyetola, made the call while leading Nigeria’s delegation to the 138th session of the International Maritime Organisation (IMO) Council in London. Oyetola, in a statement by his Special Adviser, Bolaji Akinola, said developing maritime countries must have access to technical expertise, institutional support and investment opportunities to compete effectively in the evolving global shipping industry. “Nigeria is committed to building a competitive and sustainable blue economy. We believe that developing maritime nations must have access to the technical expertise, institutional support and investment opportunities required to participate meaningfully in the evolving global shipping industry,” he said. The minister’s intervention comes as the IMO Council reviews financial allocations for the 2026–2027 biennium and strategic priorities for 2028–2029, providing Nigeria an opportunity to push for increased technical cooperation and capacity-building support. He said such support was essential to strengthening maritime institutions, improving regulatory capacity and creating an enabling environment for investment in the shipping and wider maritime sectors. Another major issue before the Council is the protection of vital international shipping routes, particularly amid growing security threats to commercial vessels in high-risk maritime zones. Under Agenda Item 11, member states are deliberating on measures to safeguard critical shipping lanes, an issue with implications for international trade, shipping costs and the movement of commercial vessels. Nigeria is expected to leverage its experience in combating piracy and maritime crime in the Gulf of Guinea to advocate stronger international cooperation and coordinated security responses. Oyetola said Nigeria’s experience had demonstrated that sustained collaboration among coastal states, international organisations and maritime stakeholders was essential to addressing maritime insecurity. “Our experience in the Gulf of Guinea has shown that maritime insecurity can be addressed through political commitment, effective coordination and cooperation among regional and international partners,” he said. The minister also stressed the need to protect seafarers, describing them as indispensable to global trade and international shipping. He said their safety, dignity and welfare must be guaranteed regardless of geopolitical tensions affecting the waters in which they operate. “Seafarers are the lifeblood of international shipping. item.title: France workers strike, march for ‘dignified wage’
item.description: Striking workers marched across France against the rising cost of living on Thursday, with hundreds of thousands of people expected to take to the streets nationwide in a new escalation following weeks of protest. The demonstrations come as the eurozone’s second largest economy battles to redress its finances, six months ahead of elections to replace centrist President Emmanuel Macron, with the far right leading in opinion polls. The high school student movement that began with youths protesting over learning conditions has coincided with widespread anger over the rising cost of living and inequality, which culminated on October 17 in the worst rioting France has seen in years. Sylvie Larneury, 61, a healthcare manager, and her 61-year-old partner, an IT specialist, were on strike Thursday so they could join the march in the central city of Clermont-Ferrand. “We’re fed up. We’re not starving, but we have to help our children even though they’ve studied,” she said. “We’ve had enough of social injustice,” she added, criticising what she called “a repressive government that defends its own interests and not those of the majority”. The unions are calling for across-the-board wage raises, tax reforms and better learning conditions for young people and have complained about police restrictions on certain protests. Protesting in the city of Lyon, winegrower Martin Thiberge said he wanted to take part in demonstrations he saw as drawing together people from across French society. “We want to make a living from our work, to make a dignified wage,” he said. Authorities estimated some 500,000 to 700,000 people would protest across the country on Thursday, while as many as 80,000 people were expected to march from 2:00 pm (1300 GMT) in the capital Paris. Unions hoped for a turnout comparable to France’s pension reform protests in 2023 that saw over one million people march. – School blockades – Dozens of high-schoolers protested in several cities, with the government reporting blockades at 81 out of the country’s 3,700 high schools. A high school student association said classes had been suspended at 1,000 such secondary schools, including those blockaded and those closed on a day of strikes. Around 16 percent of teachers nationwide were on strike, the education ministry said. In Paris, police used tear gas to try to prevent students from blocking access to the Helene-Boucher high school, an AFP reporter said. Public and private education unions have called for strike action, as well as unions representing rail workers, public hospitals and postal services. Train travel experienced some disruption on Monday morning. item.title: Otu condemns attack on Obi’s convoy, orders arrests
item.description: By Ike Uchechukwu, Calabar Cross River State Governor, Senator Bassey Otu, has condemned the attack on the convoy of the Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC) presidential candidate, Mr Peter Obi, in Calabar, directing security agencies to identify and arrest those responsible. The governor, in a statement issued by his Chief Press Secretary, Mr Linus Obogo, expressed sadness over the incident, which occurred on Wednesday during Obi’s campaign visit to the state capital. He also extended his sympathy to the former Anambra State governor and members of his entourage. “I extend my deepest, most heartfelt sympathies to Mr Peter Obi and his team over the deeply disturbing incident that occurred yesterday during his campaign visit to our state capital,” Otu said. The governor said Cross River stood in solidarity with political actors seeking to engage the electorate peacefully, stressing that no one should be intimidated or prevented from exercising their political rights. He described the attack as contrary to the state’s reputation for hospitality and peaceful coexistence, saying it did not reflect the values of its people. “Cross River has long been cherished as the cradle of hospitality, warmth and civil decorum in Nigeria; our culture is rooted in peace, harmony and mutual respect for all people, regardless of political affiliation,” he said. Otu said the incident was unacceptable and assured political parties that the state remained open to peaceful and lawful political activities. He warned that his administration would not tolerate political violence or criminality in any form. “Let it be made unmistakably clear: our administration maintains a zero-tolerance stance against political violence and criminality in any form,” he said. The governor disclosed that he had directed security agencies to track down those responsible for the attack and ensure they were brought to justice. “I have directed our security agencies to leave no stone unturned, until every single perpetrator of this shameful act is brought to book to face the full weight of the law,” Otu said. item.title: Eisenkot tipped to seek Israel government as religious party drops Netanyahu
item.description: Gadi Eisenkot emerged on Thursday as the favourite to be tasked with trying to form an Israeli government as a religious party long aligned with Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu declined to recommend him. President Isaac Herzog was holding a second day of consultations with political parties after the October 27 election, in which neither Netanyahu — a polarising right-winger who has led Israel through three years of war — nor Eisenkot — a former military chief promising to restore national unity — secured enough votes for a majority. Herzog will choose by himself whom to ask to form a new government but traditionally the mandate is given to the person recommended by more parties, which would be Eisenkot. The opposition leader also received a recommendation from a key lawmaker from the Israeli-Arab minority, whose seats in parliament soared due to outrage over Netanyahu’s policies, even as Eisenkot has remained unclear on whether he would accept Arab support to form a government. United Torah Judaism, which backed Netanyahu after the previous five elections, in its meeting with Herzog declined to recommend Netanyahu again as prime minister, although it also did not side with Eisenkot. The party informed Herzog “that it has decided not to recommend any member of Knesset to form a government,” the president’s office said in a statement, referring to the 120-member parliament in which United Torah Judaism has won seven seats. The party — which represents ultra-Orthodox Jews of Ashkenazi origin, who mostly hail from or have roots in Europe — as well as Shas — which represents the same community but of Sephardic, or mostly Middle Eastern and North African descent — have both been backed by Netanyahu as they push to maintain the exemption from military service for religious students. Netanyahu has preserved the exemption but stopped short of enshrining it in law, in the face of major resentment from many other Israelis as reservists serve multiple tours due to the wars in Gaza, Lebanon and Iran. “In whatever government is next formed, our immediate item is sorting out the status of Torah students,” United Torah Judaism lawmaker Isaac Pindrus said. Eisenkot, who has tried to appeal to secular Israelis from left to right, has been adamant about closing exemptions to military service. Some of his opposition allies have criticised the ultra-Orthodox, who make up about 14 percent of the population but have far higher birthrates than secular Israelis, as a drain on the state. Observers say United Torah Judaism’s tactic is likely aimed mostly at punishing Netanyahu and showing that their votes cannot be taken for granted, while they would still serve in a government if he were to form one. – Arab-Israelis play key role – Once Herzog gives his mandate to a lawmaker, the person — presumably either Eisenkot or Netanyahu — will have 28 days to form a government, with a potential 14-day extension. If the lawmaker fails, Herzog will then task someone else. Netanya

item.title: Edo Moves To Launch State-Owned Airline As Okpebholo Signs MoU
item.description: Edo State Governor, Monday Okpebholo, moved a step closer to establishing a state-owned airline on Wednesday by signing a Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) with China Express Airline Co. Ltd and KDN Aero. The governor signed the agreement at Government House, Benin City, with representatives of the Chinese airline led by its President, Shansheng Li, following a presentation on the company’s operational capacity. He said the carrier would be operating “very soon.” Expressing satisfaction with the proposed partnership and describing the MoU as the beginning of a longer relationship, Okpebholo said, “We have signed the MoU, and this is the first part of it. We will continue to build on it. “A presentation was made, which was very beautiful and wonderful. We have seen your capability, and we are ready to do business with you. By the grace of God, Edo Air will be in the airspace very soon. item.title: Leave EFCC out of politics, Kogi group warns Obi-Kwankwaso Movement
item.description: By John Alechenu ABUJA — The Kogi Central Progressive Elites have warned the Obi-Kwankwaso Movement against dragging the Economic and Financial Crimes Commission (EFCC) into partisan politics following its call for an investigation into Senator Natasha Akpoti-Uduaghan’s recent cash empowerment programme. The group described the call as a politically motivated attempt to undermine the lawmaker ahead of the 2027 general elections. In a statement issued in Abuja on Thursday, its President, Abdullahi Omeiza, said the group was concerned about what it described as the growing tendency among political actors to deploy anti-corruption institutions and rhetoric for partisan purposes. He said: “We are concerned about the growing tendency among some political actors to deploy anti-corruption institutions and rhetoric as instruments of partisan warfare. “Accountability is important, but it must be pursued through facts, evidence and established legal procedures, not through sensational political narratives designed to damage the reputation of an elected public official.” The group argued that constituency empowerment programmes should not automatically be classified as vote-buying simply because they involve direct financial assistance to beneficiaries. It said such initiatives could be subjected to legitimate scrutiny, but insisted that any investigation must be guided by evidence and the law. “The mere distribution of financial assistance to constituents does not, in itself, establish an offence of vote-buying,” the statement added. On the demand for an EFCC investigation and prosecution, the group acknowledged that no one was above the law but cautioned against turning anti-corruption agencies into instruments of political intimidation. Omeiza said: “Accountability is indispensable to democratic governance, but it must never become a convenient weapon for settling political scores. “Allegations are not convictions, petitions are not proof of wrongdoing, and public accusations cannot substitute for due process. “The EFCC must be allowed to discharge its statutory responsibilities independently, without being subjected to political pressure or media-driven prejudgement.” The group challenged the Obi-Kwankwaso Movement to submit any credible evidence to the appropriate authorities rather than rely on public declarations and what it described as inflammatory narratives. It also maintained that the people of Kogi Central had the right to assess Akpoti-Uduaghan’s performance and determine whether she deserved another term. “The people of Kogi Central are politically conscious, discerning and capable of evaluating their representative. They understand the difference between constructive criticism and politically motivated attacks. “No pressure group, political organisation or individual can arrogate to itself the authority to determine the political destiny of our senatorial district,” Omeiza said. item.title: Kidnappers demand N25m for nine corps members, driver abducted in Ogun
item.description: By Adeola Badru Families of 10 travellers, including nine members of the National Youth Service Corps (NYSC) and a driver, have appealed to the Federal Government and security agencies to secure their release after they were abducted along the Ijebu-Ode–Ibadan road in Ogun State. The kidnappers have demanded a ransom of N25 million and reportedly given the families a Thursday deadline to pay. One of the victims, identified as Dapo, is a recently discharged corps member who completed his national service in Edo State last week. He was reportedly travelling to Ibadan when the incident occurred on Tuesday. His sister, Abigeal, who raised the alarm, said the family had been thrown into distress following the abduction, particularly as they lacked the means to raise the demanded ransom. According to her, the victims were travelling from Ijebu-Ode towards Ibadan when their vehicle was attacked shortly after 7pm. She said her brother had been updating the family about his journey until he sent a video showing the traffic situation on the road, which turned out to be their last communication with him. Abigeal said the family learnt of the abduction after one of the corps members travelling in the vehicle escaped and contacted another family member shortly after 7pm on Tuesday. She said: “On Tuesday, my brother was on his way back from Edo. He was posted to Edo State for NYSC and did his passing-out ceremony last week. So, he was on his way back to Ibadan. “He was still giving us updates about his journey. At some point, he posted that there was traffic. I have the videos on my phone. That was the last time we heard from him. “Not until around past 7pm, when one of the corps members escaped. I don’t know how he escaped. “I also spoke to that guy yesterday. He was the one who told another brother of mine that their bus was attacked and they had been kidnapped, my brother and nine other people.” She said the family was informed that police officers and local vigilantes had launched a search operation in the forest shortly after the incident but expressed concern that the operation had yet to yield any breakthrough. According to her, the family visited the Ijebu-Ode Police Station on Wednesday to report the incident and seek information about the victims. She said the police initially asked them to remain calm, explaining that their personnel were still searching the forest. However, the operatives reportedly returned less than an hour later without any information about the abducted travellers. Abigeal said the family was subsequently advised to await contact from the kidnappers. She said that while they were returning from the police station to the motor park, the abductors called using her brother’s mobile phone. The family reportedly returned to the police station, where they heard Dapo’s voice before the kidnappers took over the conversation and demanded N20 million. item.title: UK to hold talks on harms of slave trade
item.description: Commonwealth leaders have welcomed Britain’s agreement to engage in “time-bound inclusive and good-faith dialogue” over the “historical harms” of the transatlantic slave trade. In a final communique issued late on Wednesday, the group of nations said the time had come for “meaningful, truthful and respectful conversation towards forging a common future based on equity”. But it did not set out a timetable for the talks. It comes after British Prime Minister Andy Burnham said he was open to saying sorry but ruled out paying financial reparations demanded by some Caribbean countries. Burnham used his appearance at the Commonwealth Heads of Government Meeting in Antigua and Barbuda to hold discussions about issuing a formal apology for Britain’s role in slavery, which saw about 10-15 million slaves brought from Africa to the Americas over four centuries. In a speech to opening the biannual Commonwealth leaders meeting on Tuesday, King Charles III, who is politically neutral, called the slave trade “a monstrous injustice” that filled him with “profound personal sorrow”, stopping short of a formal apology. Britain’s pivotal part in slavery has long strained relations between the UK and its former colonies, including an awkward previous meeting of Commonwealth leaders in 2024. “We welcome the agreement of the government of the United Kingdom to engage in a structured, time-bound, inclusive and good-faith dialogue with affected parties addressing the transatlantic trafficking of enslaved Africans and its historical harms,” the final communique said. The Commonwealth is a 56-nation group of mostly former British colonies. Of those Charles remains head of state in 14. Britain’s Foreign Secretary Ed Miliband has said it is “not feasible” for the country to pay reparations for slavery, but that “there are things we can work on co-operatively”. Miliband also hinted that Britain could issue a formal apology next year when it hosts a G20 leaders’ summit, in comments to the BBC aired on Wednesday as the meeting wrapped up. item.title: KEDI Healthcare Celebrates 20 Years in Nigeria with 8th Car Award Ceremony and Major Announcements
item.description: KEDI Healthcare Industries Nigeria Limited celebrated its 20th anniversary alongside its 8th Car Award Ceremony on 24 October 2026 at the Wole Soyinka Centre for Culture and the Creative Arts (formerly the National Theatre), Iganmu, Lagos. Held under the theme “A Grand Celebration of Excellence & Global Impact” and the slogan “BIGGER. BETTER. GREATER.”, the event brought together distributors, business partners, distinguished guests and stakeholders from Nigeria and other African countries to celebrate two decades of growth, entrepreneurship and community impact. Recognizing Excellence and Distributor Achievements The highlight of the celebration was KEDI’s 8th Car Award Ceremony, recognizing outstanding distributors for their business achievements and contributions to the company’s growth. The ceremony celebrated Car Awardees from Nigeria and Ghana, alongside distributors recognized across various categories, including outstanding consultants, managers, directors, service centres, lecturers and business teams. Special recognition was given to KEDI’s three Honorary Chairmen — Chief Chinedu Sunny Ojiaku, Mr. Adegbemisoye Zion and Mr. Ajala Eniola — for their exceptional contributions to the company’s development. Through its recognition programmes, business training and distributor support initiatives, KEDI continues to encourage entrepreneurship, leadership development and long-term business growth. Celebrating 20 Years and Unveiling a Renewed Corporate Direction Established in 2006, KEDI Healthcare has developed a strong presence in Nigeria and expanded its business network into other African markets, including Ghana, Benin Republic and Liberia. During the anniversary celebration, KEDI’s Operations Director, Mr. Roger Luo, acknowledged the contributions of distributors, employees and business partners throughout the company’s 20-year journey. He also introduced KEDI’s renewed corporate mission and vision, reflecting the company’s ambition to combine traditional medicine wisdom with modern health and beauty solutions while empowering business partners through opportunities for growth and shared prosperity. The company’s new vision is “To become the world’s most trusted health and wellness platform, empowering lives with total well-being, success, and vitality.” The event also introduced Road to Africa , a book written by KEDI’s Founder and Chairman, Mr. William Zhao, documenting his experiences and entrepreneurial journey in Africa. The Chinese edition has been published, with an English edition expected to follow. Aloe House: Expanding into Beauty and Wellness Another major announcement was the unveiling of Aloe House, a new beauty and wellness project developed through a partnership between KEDI Healthcare and AGHG in the United States. item.title: Kane becomes highest-paid footballer in Europe after new deal
item.description: England captain Harry Kane has signed a record-breaking contract extension with Bayern Munich that will keep him at the German club until June 2029, in a deal reportedly making him the highest-paid player in Europe by basic salary. According to David Ornstein of The Athletic , the three-year extension is the most lucrative contract in Bayern Munich’s history, although some European players could still earn more than the striker when performance-related bonuses are included. The 33-year-old’s previous contract was due to expire next summer, but both Kane and the Bundesliga champions were keen to continue their partnership. Bayern reportedly do not consider the new agreement his final contract, with the club keen to retain the England international for the foreseeable future. Speaking after signing the extension, Kane expressed his satisfaction with life in Munich, describing his relationship with the club, supporters and city as a special one. “I feel right at home at FC Bayern. I love the club, the fans and the city of Munich,” he said. “We have a fantastic team and, in Vincent Kompany, a fantastic manager. It makes me very proud to be part of this club. My whole family is very happy here. I was keen to stay. “I’m now looking forward to the future and I want to win many more titles with this great club.” The contract extension comes after a remarkable period for the striker, who won the Ballon d’Or in late October, becoming the first English player to receive the prestigious award since 2001. He is also expected to become England’s most-capped player during the November international break. Since joining Bayern from Tottenham Hotspur three years ago, Kane has scored 156 goals in 161 appearances, establishing himself as one of the club’s most influential players. During his time in Germany, he has won two Bundesliga titles, the DFB-Pokal and two Supercups. However, winning the UEFA Champions League remains a major ambition for the England captain as he looks to add Europe’s biggest club competition to his collection of honours. His decision to extend his stay in Germany also appears to have dealt a significant blow to hopes of him returning to the Premier League to challenge Alan Shearer’s all-time scoring record. With his Bayern future secured until 2029, Kane looks increasingly likely to prioritise further success in Germany over a return to English football.
